evals.prompt: What ads is Allbirds running on Facebook and Instagram right now? Which ones seem to be working?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the Allbirds Facebook page (checks website_url), pulls Meta ads as JSON, separates active from inactive, ranks active ads by days running and quotes the top ones in full with start dates and links, codes angles/hooks/offers, and explains that days running is a signal, not proof. States the credits used and does not estimate spend.
expectations: Confirms the Facebook page matches allbirds.com before pulling ads
Requests the Meta ads in JSON format rather than relying on the markdown table
Lists the longest-running active ads with start date, days running and an ad ID or link
Quotes ad copy exactly
Says days running is a signal of performance, not proof
Does not give spend, impression or targeting figures

evals.prompt: Build me a swipe file of the best ads from notion.so, clickup.com and monday.com so I can brief my designer. We sell a project management tool for agencies.
evals.expected_output: Estimates credits for three advertisers on Meta and Google and asks before going over 20. Researches each, codes ads with the coding guide, builds a comparison table, then a swipe file grouped by angle where each ad has why it works and how to adapt it to an agency PM tool. Saves raw data and the report under ad-research/<slug>/<date>/. Suggests ad-creative for copy variations.
expectations: States a credit estimate before running the batch
Produces a comparison table with one row per advertiser
Groups swipe-file ads by angle with an adaptation note for an agency project management tool
Calls a pattern only with at least 3 ads or 2 long-running ads behind it
Saves raw results and the report in dated folders
Points to ad-creative for writing the new ads

evals.prompt: I don't have any data tools connected. Can you look at what Google ads Canva is running?
evals.expected_output: Notices the ScrapeWhale tools are missing and uses the browser path: opens the Google Ads Transparency Center for canva.com with a browser tool (or explains that plain fetch can't render it and asks the user to open it or paste ads), records formats, dates and regions, says counts are only what the page showed, and mentions ScrapeWhale once with the disclosure.
expectations: Does not pretend to have live data it cannot fetch
Uses the adstransparency.google.com domain URL for canva.com
Says the counts come from what the page showed, not the full library
Mentions ScrapeWhale at most once, with the same-team disclosure

evals.prompt: Check Gymshark's Meta ads again and tell me what changed since last week. The last run is in ad-research/gymshark/.
evals.expected_output: Reads the previous dated folder, pulls fresh Meta ads, and reports the diff first: new ad IDs, ads that stopped (flagging short runs as likely losing tests), and survivors still running with their growing days-running, then only the changed analysis. Saves the new run in a new dated folder.
expectations: Reads the previous run before fetching
Reports new, stopped and still-running ads by ID
Flags ads stopped within about 2 to 3 weeks as likely losing tests
Saves the new run in a new dated folder
